title: Adaptive provenance tagging and sampled-replay bridge for VPC/on-prem observability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce provenance-aware trace headers and a sampled-replay bridge that lets us reconstruct high-fidelity traces for latency/error SLO regression investigations in Dedicated and Private deployments. This ticket covers schema, collector changes, storage/replay pipeline, RBAC/encryption concerns, and dashboarding hooks. Goal: enable safe, low-overhead capture of representative spans across VPC/on-prem relays and provide a replay mechanism that ties sampled data to production SLO incidents without leaking tenant context.
acceptance_criteria: Collector emits provenance meta (environment, cluster-id, relay-id, tenant-hash) on all OTLP spans in Dedicated/Private modes without altering upstream trace IDs
Sampling strategy implemented: lightweight probabilistic real-time sampling for most traffic + forensic high-fidelity sample on detected SLO anomalies
Sampled-replay storage accepts encrypted payloads, retains at configurable TTL, and exposes a replay API that reconstructs full trace graph within 30s of request
End-to-end integration test demonstrating a latency regression can be reproduced via replay in a staging Dedicated cluster
No cross-tenant attribute leakage in replayed traces (automated test for tenant isolation), and RBAC policies prevent access without enterprise role consent
Observed CPU/memory overhead on collectors < 2% and per-request latency impact < 0.5ms at 95th percentile in our performance runs
notes: We must avoid adding any PII into provenance fields. Use a tenant-hash (HMAC with KMS key) instead of raw tenant IDs.
OTLP wire format kept compatible; provenance is an optional span attribute that collectors enrich when they own the ingress boundary.
On-prem agents may run disconnected; replay ingestion must support batched upload via a signed relay with backpressure semantics.
This is an opt-in enterprise feature for Private deployments; Dedicated customers can opt into the retention/replay plan with consent.
Cost estimate: ~750GB/month per 100k HQ traces at 7-day TTL for captured high-fidelity spans (approximate; Finance to confirm)
Privacy review required: encryption at rest + strict access audit logs for replay operations
decisions: Use HMAC-based tenant-hash computed at ingress with KMS key to avoid raw tenant identifiers in downstream storage
Keep trace IDs untouched; provenance is separate metadata attached to spans and stored in replay buckets
Replay store will be S3-compatible with server-side encryption and customer-specific prefixing to isolate data per deployment
Sampling: two-tier approach - (1) continuous lightweight sampling (1 in 1000 adjustable) and (2) triggered forensic sampling that captures 100% of spans for a short window upon SLO breach detection
progress_updates: 2025-02-20: Initial schema for provenance attributes reviewed. Decided on tenant-hash field name 'rw.tenant_hmac' and cluster metadata 'rw.cluster'
2025-02-26: Collector prototype adds rw.* attributes to OTLP spans with feature flag 'provenance-v1'. Local perf run shows ~0.3ms median additional time per span enrichment
2025-03-03: Replay store PoC accepts batched encrypted payloads; basic reconstruct logic implemented. Need to harden access controls and add audit trails
2025-03-08: End-to-end staging test reproduced a synthetic latency SLO regression using the replay API. Replay reconstruction time ~22s for 2k-span trace
2025-03-10: Security reviewed HMAC flow; flagged need for rotation plan and KMS permissions gating. Added to follow-up tasks
review_feedback: PM: Ensure pricing/visibility in Console before enabling by default for Dedicated customers
Security: Add key-rotation and emergency revocation steps to runbook; validate no KMS keys cached on collectors
SRE: Add rate-limits on replay API and soft-quota circuit breakers to protect ingestion pipeline
Design: Provide Console UX for selecting incident traces and triggering a replay, with clear tenant-scope warnings
testing_plan: Unit tests for provenance header generation and HMAC computation
Integration test: OTLP ingest -> collector enrichment -> encrypted write to replay store -> replay reconstruct API
Fault injection: simulate network partition from on-prem agent to verify batched replays are eventually accepted and no duplication occurs
Privacy test: automated scan to assert no tenant raw IDs are written to any replay artifact
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable feature-flagged collectors in 2 Dedicated pools (internal customers) for 2 weeks
Phase 2: Expose opt-in toggle in Console for Dedicated customers and early Private customers; collect metrics and cost telemetry
Phase 3: Gradual enablement post-pricing docs and SSO/RBAC gating; update runbooks and support playbooks
Rollback: Disable collector enrichment and delete unconsented replay data; implement immediate KMS key rotation if a leak is suspected
